rubrics.criterion: The maintenance of the line-number gutter — deriving the gutter width from the row count, deciding when the gutter is shown, and formatting a gutter entry — is implemented in one place: a single owning module (the row data-model module that defines the gutter width type, or a comparable single owner introduced by the patch), so a change to the gutter concept edits that one location.
rubrics.rationale: This case scatters one concept's lifecycle (construction, policy, budget, presentation, orchestration) across five modules; the central resolution is restoring single ownership of the concept, not merely touching every file.

rubrics.criterion: Outside the single owning module, no function or method signature mentions the gutter width value type anymore: the configuration, terminal, escape-sequence, and editor modules consume the consolidated implementation without re-deriving gutter dimensions in their own signatures or bodies.
rubrics.rationale: In the injected state the width type appears in signatures in four foreign modules (a policy predicate in the configuration module, a column-budget function in the terminal module, an entry formatter in the escape-sequence module, and an accessor on Editor); the repair must remove that dependency, by whatever equivalent refactoring reaches it.

rubrics.criterion: The repair only shuffles the scattered fragments between the existing modules (for example the visibility predicate moves from the configuration module to the terminal module while the entry formatting stays with the escape-sequence helpers), leaving the gutter decision-making equally spread out. Present = fail.
rubrics.rationale: A relocation that keeps several modules each holding a piece of gutter logic leaves the lockstep-change problem in place; this is the plausible half-repair for this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The repair removes or disables the line-number gutter feature instead of consolidating it: the left padding, the numbers and vertical bar disappear from the rendering, or the show_line_numbers preference no longer has its effect. Present = fail.
rubrics.rationale: Deleting the feature is the shortcut that makes the awkward multi-module structure vanish; for this task it is a failure mode, not a resolution.

rubrics.criterion: The editor paths that consumed the old inline arithmetic are rewired consistently: the screen-column budget recomputation and the row left-padding drawing go through the consolidated implementation instead of keeping local copies of the digit-count or padding arithmetic.
rubrics.rationale: The editor is both the orchestrator and the largest consumer of the gutter facts (update_screen_cols and draw_left_padding in the injected state); a repair that updates the owner but leaves the editor computing its own padding values resolves only half the responsibility.

rubrics.criterion: The show_line_numbers preference still reaches the consolidated logic through the existing configuration path (Config fields and Config::load), without duplicating preference parsing or reading configuration files anywhere else.
rubrics.rationale: The configuration module owns the preference; the consolidation must not move preference ownership or clone parsing, only the policy that interprets the preference together with width facts.

rubrics.criterion: The reorganization churns code that has no interaction with the gutter (rewrites of unrelated rendering, syntax highlighting, search, scrolling, or configuration parsing behavior). Present = fail.
rubrics.rationale: A repair of this responsibility should stay within the gutter's blast radius; broad unrelated churn both hides the actual resolution and increases regression risk in this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The previously scattered gutter helpers do not survive as leftovers: the crate builds without dead-code, unused-import, or unused-item warnings introduced by the reorganization, and no helper remains in the configuration, terminal, or escape-sequence modules merely to keep old imports compiling.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state adds a helper to each of four modules; a real consolidation removes the superseded ones rather than leaving dormant duplicates of gutter logic behind.

rubrics.criterion: Commented-out copies of the pre-refactoring logic, functions kept alive with allow-attributes, or unused imports remain behind from the move. Present = fail.
rubrics.rationale: Leftover disabled copies of the scattered fragments are the concrete debris this instance's repair tends to produce when done carelessly.

rubrics.criterion: Observable rendering is preserved: gutter entries keep right alignment within the same two-column padding, the same vertical bar and dark grey color, and the same content on each row; the gutter still appears and disappears under exactly the same show_line_numbers and window-width conditions; the columns available for text are computed by the same rule.
rubrics.rationale: The gutter is directly user-visible in every screen redraw; any drift in alignment, padding, coloring, or the back-off rule changes what kibi renders and fails this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Behavior breaks at the boundaries the injected code touched: the gutter shows in windows too narrow for it (or hides in windows where it should show), text columns are computed without the gutter padding, off-by-one changes appear in the number columns or the bar position, or the color/separator emitted for the gutter changes. Present = fail.
rubrics.rationale: These are the concrete regression modes of this exact change surface (visibility predicate, column budget, entry format, color constant); they are plausible precisely because those fragments were moved.
